title: Payment service slow responses
executive_summary: Payment-service p99 rose from ~300ms to ~3.4s and timeout rate from 0.1% to ~6% starting 18:09-18:10Z. Payment's own CPU, DB connection utilisation, Redis and Postgres were all unchanged, so the pods look healthy because the bottleneck is upstream. Auth-service degraded first (p99 from ~90ms to ~4s, error rate 0.3% to ~2.9%, CPU 30% to ~47%, queue times up to 9.7s), starting 18:07-18:08Z. Auth logs show slow JWKS refreshes from identity-provider. Payment's errors are "Upstream timeout calling auth-service after 3000ms" and slow verify calls. Historical incident HIST-2025-031 matches this pattern, but it is an analogy only.

hypotheses.description: auth-service is saturated or stalled, likely because of slow JWKS/identity-provider calls, causing queueing on /v1/token/verify that propagates as timeouts to payment-service. root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): upstream_dependency_degradation in auth-service - auth-service is saturated or stalled, likely because of slow JWKS/identity-provider calls, causing queueing on /v1/token/verify that propagates as timeouts to payment-service.
corrective_actions: Mitigate auth-service: scale out replicas or shed load on /v1/token/verify.
Engage identity-provider owners to check JWKS endpoint latency and availability.
Revert payment-service log.level from DEBUG to INFO (OPS-2898) to remove unnecessary load.
preventive_actions: Add timeouts, retries with backoff, and a circuit breaker around payment's auth calls, so a slow auth-service fails fast instead of holding threads.
Cache JWKS keys with a longer TTL and stale-while-revalidate, so identity-provider slowness does not block token verification.
Add identity-provider to the monitored service catalog.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on auth-service p99 and queue time for /v1/token/verify.
Alert on JWKS refresh duration from identity-provider.
Dashboard payment timeouts split by upstream dependency, so the upstream cause is visible from the payment dashboard.
limitations: Timing correlation between auth and payment onset is about 1-2 minutes, so causation is inferred from the dependency direction and log messages, not proven.

conclusion: Payment-service latency and timeouts are downstream effects of degraded auth-service (/v1/token/verify). Auth-service degraded first (~18:07-18:08Z, p99 and error-rate onset), about 1-2 minutes before payment-service's onset at 18:09-18:10Z. Auth logs show request queueing and slow JWKS refreshes from identity-provider, which points to an upstream identity-provider slowdown as the likely trigger. identity-provider is not a monitored service, so this link is unconfirmed. The DEBUG log-level change on payment-service is not supported as the cause: payment CPU and DB pool are flat, and the change precedes onset by ~35 minutes.
